mechanism: Threshold monotonicity for over/under markets on the same numeric quantity. For any two binary markets on the same underlying statistic (e.g., team points, game total points, player yards) with thresholds X < Y, the event 'statistic > Y' logically implies 'statistic > X'. Therefore the YES price of the higher-threshold market must be less than or equal to the YES price of the lower-threshold market. If p(Y) > p(X), sell the higher-threshold YES and buy the lower-threshold YES to lock a risk-free profit.
counterparty: Traders who misprice nested threshold events, e.g., pricing a more extreme over at higher probability than a less extreme over on the same numeric quantity.
why_not_arbitraged: In an efficient market, monotonicity is enforced by arbitrageurs; any violation is immediately traded away. The relation is a pure logical implication, not a statistical prediction.
falsification: Finding any pair of over/under markets on the same numeric quantity with thresholds X < Y where the YES price for the higher threshold exceeds the YES price for the lower threshold by more than transaction costs.
target_market: Any pair of binary over/under markets on the same numeric quantity with ordered thresholds.

Replace placeholders with the actual YES tokens of the higher-threshold and lower-threshold markets respectively. Scope 'all' means this applies to every matching pair of markets.
